finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: POST /hooks/test passes attacker-supplied req.body.callback directly to axios.post, with no validation, and returns the upstream status.
finding.source: req.body.callback (HTTP JSON request body, any client reaching the pub router)

trace.note: pub = express.Router() created with no auth middleware
req.body.callback used as URL for outbound POST, no validation
upstream HTTP status returned to caller

finding.guards_checked: None. No scheme, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local block, port restriction, or redirect control. Axios follows redirects by default. Caveat: pub mounting and req.body parser are configured outside this repo.

verdict.guard_found: none in routes.js: no validation of req.body.callback before axios.post at routes.js:20; requireAdmin (routes.js:7-12) is applied only to the admin router, not pub
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:4, 19, 20, 21 match the claim) and no closing guard exists, but the only file available is routes.js, so whether `pub` is mounted behind authentication or a body parser is configured (both outside this directory) cannot be determined; if `pub` is mounted publicly with a JSON body parser, the finding is CONFIRMED.

finding.claim: SSRF in admin diagnostics: GET /diagnostics/fetch passes req.query.url directly to axios.get and returns the status. Only the admin role check guards it.
finding.source: req.query.url (query-string parameter supplied by the requester)

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applied to all admin routes
req.query.url passed to axios.get with no validation

finding.guards_checked: Admin role check only (routes.js:7-10). URL not validated; redirects followed by default. Session population is configured outside this repo.

verdict.guard_found: routes.js:12 admin.use(requireAdmin) and routes.js:7-8 role check (req.session.role !== "admin" returns 403). No URL/hostname validation before axios.get at routes.js:15, and redirects are followed by default.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12, 7-8, 15, 16), but the value reaching the sink at routes.js:15 is only controllable by a caller who already holds the admin role, which routes.js:8 enforces; that is not the low-privilege or unauthenticated attacker the source criterion requires, so this is an admin-only SSRF rather than a finding.
